problemStatement.formal: For a bounded operator T on an inner-product space over an RCLike field, ‖⟪T x, y⟫‖ ≤ ‖T‖·‖x‖·‖y‖; and for a positive symmetric T, ⟪T x, y⟫² ≤ ⟪T x, x⟫·⟪T y, y⟫.
problemStatement.plain: Sharpen Cauchy–Schwarz when one vector is the image of a bounded operator T: the inner product is controlled by the operator norm. Develop the numerical-radius bound, submultiplicativity, the adjoint form, recovery of classical Cauchy–Schwarz, and the positive-operator (Kadison–Schwarz) inequality.
whyMatters: Connects the elementary Cauchy–Schwarz inequality to operator theory (numerical radius, Kadison–Schwarz) over a general RCLike field (ℝ or ℂ).
Shows operator-norm Cauchy–Schwarz is one substitution away from the scalar case, and that a positive symmetric operator induces its own semi-inner-product Cauchy–Schwarz.

proven: Operator-norm Cauchy–Schwarz ‖⟪T x, y⟫‖ ≤ ‖T‖·‖x‖·‖y‖ over any RCLike field.
Numerical-radius bound ‖⟪T x, x⟫‖ ≤ ‖T‖·‖x‖² (w(T) ≤ ‖T‖); submultiplicativity under composition and scaling; adjoint form.
Recovery of classical scalar Cauchy–Schwarz from the identity operator (‖id‖ ≤ 1).
Positive-operator (Kadison–Schwarz) inequality ⟪T x, y⟫² ≤ ⟪T x, x⟫·⟪T y, y⟫ for positive symmetric T, plus its square-root form, via a discriminant argument.
knownResults.goal: Formalize the operator-norm and positive-operator strengthenings of Cauchy–Schwarz and recover the classical inequality as a special case.

builtItems: operator_cauchy_schwarz: ‖⟪T x, y⟫‖ ≤ ‖T‖·‖x‖·‖y‖ for a bounded operator T over any RCLike field (substitute ‖T x‖ ≤ ‖T‖·‖x‖ into scalar Cauchy–Schwarz).
operator_numerical_radius_bound: ‖⟪T x, x⟫‖ ≤ ‖T‖·‖x‖² — numerical radius dominated by operator norm (y = x specialization).
operator_cs_comp / operator_cs_smul: submultiplicativity of the bound under operator composition and scalar multiplication.
operator_cs_adjoint: adjoint form ‖⟪T† y, x⟫‖ ≤ ‖T‖·‖y‖·‖x‖ via ⟪T† y, x⟫ = ⟪y, T x⟫; recovers_classical_cs: identity operator recovers scalar ‖⟪x, y⟫‖ ≤ ‖x‖·‖y‖.
positive_operator_cauchy_schwarz + positive_operator_cs_abs: Kadison–Schwarz ⟪T x, y⟫² ≤ ⟪T x, x⟫·⟪T y, y⟫ for positive symmetric T (discriminant of a nonnegative quadratic), and the √ form.
insights: Operator-norm Cauchy–Schwarz is one substitution from the scalar case: replace ‖T x‖ by its defining bound ‖T‖·‖x‖.
The numerical radius w(T) = sup over unit x of ‖⟪T x, x⟫‖ is dominated by the operator norm — the y = x specialization.
A positive symmetric operator turns ⟪T x, y⟫ into a semi-inner product, so it satisfies its own (commutative Kadison–Schwarz) Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.

The discriminant trick: a quadratic in t nonnegative everywhere has b² − 4ac ≤ 0, which IS Cauchy–Schwarz for the form ⟨·,·⟩_T; composition (‖S T‖ ≤ ‖S‖·‖T‖) and scaling, with ‖id‖ ≤ 1, recover the classical case.
